name: Computer Networking
description: Understanding how data moves across networks, including IP addressing, subnetting, TCP/UDP, DNS and the OSI/TCP-IP models.

resources.title: Khan Academy: Computers and the Internet

questions.question: What is the main job of DNS?
options: Translating domain names into IP addresses
questions.explanation: DNS resolves human-readable names like example.com to IP addresses; DHCP assigns addresses.

questions.question: What is the default TCP port for HTTPS?
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses 443; 80 is HTTP, 21 is FTP and 22 is SSH.

questions.question: Which statement correctly contrasts TCP and UDP?
options: TCP is connection-oriented with reliable, ordered delivery; UDP is connectionless with no delivery guarantees
UDP guarantees ordering; TCP does not
TCP is only used on local networks
questions.explanation: TCP provides handshakes, acknowledgements and retransmission; UDP trades those for lower overhead.

questions.question: How many usable host addresses does an IPv4 /24 subnet provide?
questions.explanation: A /24 has 256 addresses; the network and broadcast addresses are reserved, leaving 254.

questions.question: At which OSI layer does a router primarily make forwarding decisions?
questions.explanation: Routers forward packets based on IP addresses, which belong to the network layer; switches typically work at layer 2.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of the TCP three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: The client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK.

practical.title: Subnet calculation
practical.instructions: For the host 192.168.10.37/26, state the subnet mask in dotted-decimal form, the network address, the broadcast address and the number of usable host addresses.

rubric.hint: /26 means 26 one-bits: the last octet is 11000000 = 192.
Block size is 64, so .37 falls in the .0-.63 block.
The broadcast is the last address in the block: .63.

tasks.title: Learn how the internet works
tasks.description: Complete the Internet unit of Khan Academy's Computers and the Internet course, covering IP addresses, DNS, packets, routing, TCP/UDP and HTTP.
tasks.completion_criteria: You can explain what happens when you type a URL into a browser, step by step.

tasks.title: Explore your network with CLI tools
tasks.description: Use ipconfig/ip addr, ping, traceroute/tracert and nslookup/dig to inspect your own network and resolve a few domains. Record what each tool shows.
tasks.completion_criteria: Notes with output and explanation for each of the 4 tools.

tasks.title: Subnetting drills and packet capture
tasks.description: Solve 20 subnetting problems by hand (masks, network/broadcast addresses, host counts). Then capture your own traffic in Wireshark and identify a DNS query and a TCP handshake.
tasks.completion_criteria: 20 correct subnetting answers and annotated screenshots of a DNS exchange and a TCP handshake.

tasks.title: Design and simulate a small office network
tasks.description: Design a network for a small office with separate subnets or VLANs for staff, guests and servers, and document the addressing plan, routing and firewall rules. Build it in a network simulator or with virtual machines.
tasks.completion_criteria: An addressing plan, diagram and working simulation where guest devices cannot reach the server subnet.
